Structural Checks on a Model Term

Source: R/check_term.R
check_term.Rd

Builds term against data and runs six checks on the result: that the build succeeds and returns a two-dimensional numeric block with one row per observation, that the coefficient names are unique and as numerous as the columns, that term_npar() agrees with that count, that term_smooth() returns a single non-missing logical, that term_predict() on the same data reproduces the block, and that term_predict() on a subset of rows returns the corresponding rows of it. The result has one row per check; the rows are printed after all the checks have run, when verbose is TRUE, and returned invisibly.

The last check detects a term that rebuilds its encoding. A term is supposed to record its encoding at build time and reapply it; a term that re-derives the encoding from whatever rows it is handed passes every other check and fails this one.

Usage

check_term(term, data, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

term

A term specification: any object inheriting from additive_term(), built or unbuilt. An object that is not a model_term() signals the error "'term' must inherit from 'model_term'.", and a structural_term() is rejected by name. An already-built term is accepted and is rebuilt against data.

data

A data frame carrying every variable that the term names. Any other object signals the error "'data' must be a data frame.", and a data frame without rows signals "'data' has no rows.". With one row the subset check compares the block against itself and is uninformative.

verbose

Print one line per check once all the checks have run, TRUE by default, in the form [OK] subset -- 4 rows. The rows are returned either way, so verbose = FALSE is the form to use inside a test.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame of check, status and info, all character, one row per check:

check

"build", "names", "npar", "smooth", "reproduce" and "subset", in that order.

status

"OK" or "FAILED".

info

The block's dimensions for build, in the form "6 x 4 block", followed by ", sparse" when the block is an S4 matrix; "smooth" or "non-smooth" for smooth; the number of rows kept for subset; the condition message of a check that signaled an error; and "" otherwise.

A build that signals an error gives a single row, check = "build" and status = "FAILED", with the message in info; the later checks are not attempted.

The two identities

Write \(X\) for term_matrix(term_build(term, data)) and \(S\) for a subset of the row indices. The last two checks are

$$\mathrm{predict}(\mathrm{term}, \mathrm{data}) = X, \qquad \mathrm{predict}(\mathrm{term}, \mathrm{droplevels}(\mathrm{data}[S, ])) = X[S, ],$$

and each of them is compared by all.equal() at a relative tolerance of 1e-12. The second does not follow from the first: a term that rebuilds its encoding satisfies the first because the rows are the same ones, and fails the second as soon as \(S\) omits a factor level or narrows the range on which a basis is placed.

Which rows the subset takes

The subset is chosen to make that failure reachable. If a column of data is a factor with two or more levels whose last level occurs in some but not all of the rows, every row of that level is dropped, so a rebuilt encoding is one column short. Failing that, the first max(1, nrow(data) %/% 2) rows are taken, which still narrows the range of a numeric covariate. Character columns are not examined.

droplevels() is applied to the subset before it is passed on, because new data reach term_predict() in that form: a factor column there carries only the levels that its own rows use, and the remaining levels are recorded only in the blueprint. Without the call a plain row subset carries the original level set along with it and the check cannot fail.

What is not checked

The battery covers the design block. It does not read the penalty that a penalized term attaches or the hyperparameters that the term declares, so term_penalties() and term_hyper() are never called.

check_term() applies to an additive term and rejects a structural one by name. A structural term (gas(), regime(), and the marginal break-point terms) contributes no design columns and registers no term_matrix() method, so there is nothing for the six checks to read; the error message gives this reason and lists what such a term supplies instead, which is term_params(), term_links(), term_npar() and one of term_filter() or term_loglik(). Those are not covered by any validator.

See also

term_build() and term_predict(), the two generics that the checks compare; term_matrix() for the block itself; interpret_formula() for reading a whole formula into terms.

Examples

dd <- data.frame(x = 1:6, g = factor(rep(c("a", "b", "c"), 2)))

# A parametric block passes all six.
res <- check_term(linpar(~ x + g), dd)
#>   [OK] build -- 6 x 4 block
#>   [OK] names
#>   [OK] npar
#>   [OK] smooth -- smooth
#>   [OK] reproduce
#>   [OK] subset -- 4 rows
all(res$status == "OK")
#> [1] TRUE

# This is what the subset check tests. The chosen rows drop level "c", and
# the reapplied block keeps the four columns that the blueprint recorded.
b  <- term_build(linpar(~ x + g), dd)
nd <- droplevels(dd[c(1, 2, 4, 5), ])
levels(nd$g)
#> [1] "a" "b"
dim(term_predict(b, nd))              # 4 x 4, the blueprint's levels
#> [1] 4 4
dim(model.matrix(~ x + g, nd))        # 4 x 3, what a rebuild gives
#> [1] 4 3

# The same failure occurs for a basis: rebuilding places the knots on the
# narrower range, so the columns are different functions of x.
d2  <- data.frame(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 40))
bs  <- term_build(s(x, basis7::bspline_smooth(k = 6)), d2)
X   <- term_matrix(bs)
sub <- 1:20
max(abs(term_predict(bs, d2[sub, , drop = FALSE]) - X[sub, ]))
#> [1] 0
max(abs(term_matrix(term_build(s(x, basis7::bspline_smooth(k = 6)), d2[sub, , drop = FALSE])) -
        X[sub, ]))
#> [1] 2.777484

# A sparse block is accepted, and the info column reports that it is sparse.
check_term(random(~ 1 | g), dd)
#>   [OK] build -- 6 x 3 block, sparse
#>   [OK] names
#>   [OK] npar
#>   [OK] smooth -- smooth
#>   [OK] reproduce
#>   [OK] subset -- 4 rows

# A build that fails gives one row and stops there.
print(check_term(linpar(~ x + nonexistent), dd, verbose = FALSE))
#>   check status                           info
#> 1 build FAILED object 'nonexistent' not found
